clue.text: Adult entering short run gets injury

indicators.note: the adult letter goes into the shortened run, so entering marks an insertion
short tells us to lop the last letter off the word for a run

parts.note: a sprint is a fast run
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up joins a quick dash and comes away hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SPRINT to SPRIN, and 'entering' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenched ligament, a common kind of injury to a joint.

clue.text: Religious work that is found in school group

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is sits inside the school body, so found in signals insertion

parts.note: a PTA is a Parent-Teacher Association attached to a school
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A piece of religious art turns up among a school's parent-teacher group.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a classic devotional artwork.

clue.text: Sailor needing in Le Havre a reel, say, gets plenty

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
Le Havre is in France, and the French for a is un
a reel is a Scottish folk dance, given here as an example

explanation.surface: A seaman in a French port who needs a fishing reel ends up with a good haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' suggests fishing tackle in the port scene, but 'say' flags it as an example of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful quantity, a straight synonym for plenty.

clue.text: Hold old English hero

definitions.meaning: a wrestling hold with an arm under the opponent's armpit and hand on the neck
Admiral Lord ..., the victor of Trafalgar, is a national hero of England

explanation.surface: Keep hold of a famous figure from England's past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson names both a wrestling grip and Horatio Nelson, the admiral celebrated for Trafalgar.

clue.text: English fan wearing bright colour is given snub

indicators.note: the colour is worn around the other pieces, so wearing signals one piece enclosing another

parts.note: red is a bright colour
a buff is an enthusiast or fan, as in film buff

explanation.surface: An English supporter dressed in red gets cold-shouldered.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to reject bluntly, so someone rebuffed has been given a snub.

clue.text: Terribly great intricacy about opening of negotiations? It's something guaranteed

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the single letter, so about signals enclosure
terribly suggests the words are badly arranged and need rearranging
opening of takes just the initial letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A very convoluted start to negotiations is presented as a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges GREAT INTRICACY, and 'about' wraps those letters round N, the first letter of negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing certainty is a horse certain to win, so by extension anything sure to happen.

clue.text: Musician or another heading off to tour America (New Jersey)

indicators.note: the shortened musician goes round the American letters, so to tour signals one piece around another
heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: another musician, read from the definition, is here an oboist
NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey

explanation.surface: One musician or a colleague sets off on an American tour starting in New Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows the definition: another musician, a woodwind player, whose head comes off under 'heading off' before 'to tour' wraps it round the American letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist is a banjo player, so a kind of musician.

clue.text: US actor following working lawyer there

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
on means working, as a machine that is on
there refers back to the US: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American actor tags along after a busy attorney in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry, Jane and Peter Fonda are all American actors.

clue.text: Meet chaps taking minute by bar

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the letter for minute is removed

parts.note: chaps are men
a counter is the bar over which drinks are served

explanation.surface: Arrange to meet some men grabbing a quick minute at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like adding the minute, but it means taking away; 'by' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to come across or meet them.

clue.text: Bush, maybe, cultivated in urban place (lacking a name)

indicators.note: cultivated suggests working the ground over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A shrub grown in a city spot without a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' says A and N are removed from IN URBAN PLACE; the remaining letters are rearranged by 'cultivated'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush and his father were both US presidents from the Republican Party, so Bush is an example.

clue.text: Small cut in police station

definitions.meaning: in British slang the ... is a police station or prison

explanation.surface: A minor wound picked up inside a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is both a slight cut and British slang for the police station.

clue.text: Will shown by husband with daughter now upset

parts.note: and means with, joining two things

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A will revealed by a husband and daughter causes distress today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NOW into OWN. 'Will' is the verb, as in to will property to an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand down possessions is to pass them on to heirs, which is what willing them does.

clue.text: Work by area (western half of Quebec) that's dull

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: in an across entry the western half of a word is its first half, here three letters

explanation.surface: A work set in a region of Quebec is judged boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western half of' takes QUE, the left half of QUEBEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not transparent or lacking lustre, so dull in the visual sense.

clue.text: Look over various canned drinks

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the answer is absorbed inside the words before it

explanation.surface: Examine an assortment of canned beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' looks like a noun but is the verb: the words various canned take in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to look over it quickly.

clue.text: One given lead in Mexico?

parts.note: read as a dog walked on a lead, the dog breed takes its name from a Mexican state

explanation.surface: Someone handed the lead role in a Mexican production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests the starring role, but here it is a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chihuahua is a tiny dog breed named after a state of Mexico, so it is a Mexican dog on a leash.

clue.text: Temp totally disheartened as a victim of cuts?

parts.note: a casual is a temporary worker

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart of the word, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A temporary worker who is completely downcast at being laid off in cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves TY from totally. 'cuts' suggests budget cuts, but a casualty can be anyone injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is someone injured or killed, and the question mark admits the cuts are wounds.

clue.text: A doctor for all to see with unusually clean vehicle for patients

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all audiences

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A doctor is on show with a strangely spotless vehicle for the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is a vehicle that carries the sick or injured to hospital.

clue.text: Treat leniently those initiating some offensive frivolity in British school

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the British school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: those initiating are the letters that start each of the following words

explanation.surface: Go easy on pupils starting some offensive horseplay at a British school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those initiating' refers to the leading letters of the three words after it; 'in' places them within the school name after B.
explanation.definitionFit: To be soft on someone is to deal with them too gently, an idiom for treating them leniently.

clue.text: Baron, perhaps, provided with sword is beset by extremes of laughter

indicators.note: the middle pieces are surrounded by the outer letters, so is beset by signals enclosure
extremes of takes the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A nobleman with a sword is surrounded by peals of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes L and R from laughter, which surround IF and EPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer holds a non-hereditary title, usually the rank of baron, so a baron is an example.

clue.text: Feel very hot with pain from exercise

definitions.meaning: to feel feverish or very hot
the stinging muscle pain felt during hard exercise

explanation.surface: Getting overheated and aching after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Burn means both to be extremely hot and the aching sensation athletes feel in working muscles.

clue.text: A good person retaining muscle for particular part

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the muscle goes inside

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword abbreviation for a good person
a pec is a pectoral chest muscle

explanation.surface: A virtuous person keeps hold of one particular muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one feature or facet of something, a particular part of the whole.

clue.text: Fair shot at intervals? Quite true

parts.note: just means fair, as in a just decision

indicators.note: at intervals picks every other letter from the word

explanation.surface: A reasonable attempt that happens now and then is perfectly accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so is an idiom of agreement meaning exactly right or quite true.

clue.text: Lightly touch middle of very thin candle

parts.note: to tap is to touch lightly

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Gently pat the centre of a very slender candle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes ER from very. 'very thin' suggests a description of the candle, but thin is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a slender candle or wax-coated wick used for lighting.

clue.text: Sale about to be arranged with article missing? It's fixed!

indicators.note: to be arranged tells us the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rigged sale, put together with one item gone, is exposed as a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' says A is removed from SALE ABOUT; 'to be arranged' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means fixed in the sense of unconditional and not subject to change.

clue.text: Much appreciated series? It's something stunning

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A well-loved TV run is presented as a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning' suggests dazzling, but here it means a device that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon used to stun a person temporarily.

clue.text: Disciplinarian with heavy, imposing presence at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset takes the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian makes a heavy and imposing impression from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip is the party official who enforces voting discipline in parliament.

clue.text: Sense trend that's developed to show kindly quality

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Detect an emerging fashion that shows warmth of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentleness and affection, a kindly trait.

clue.text: Old woman with turn oddly just like a nurse?

parts.note: ma is mother, and old woman is slang for one's mother

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: just means only

explanation.surface: An elderly woman with a strange turn behaves exactly like a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TR from turn. 'just' does double work in the surface but is ONLY here; the definition is 'like a nurse?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron was the senior nurse of a hospital, so matronly behaviour is like a nurse's.

clue.text: Some loathe or yearn for a system of ideas

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people hate or long for an ideology.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a set of principles explaining something, a structured system of ideas.
